title: BenchX comparison document
description: The comparator's output: verdicts for target results against their references, in history mode or run mode, with the evidence behind each. See docs/design/comparator.md section 5. Derived and recomputed on demand; the store keeps its inputs, not the document.
$comment: Rules the schema cannot express and the comparator enforces: inputs lists every result the document refers to; local_only is true when any input is not clean in subject_dirty or benchmark_dirty (benchmark-result-schema.md section 5.5); a unit affected by a failed invariant has no verdict and appears in no units entry; in history mode every reference result precedes the target under the recorded ordering.

comparison_version.description: Major version of this document contract.

mode.description: History mode compares a target series point against preceding points of its series; run mode compares two sides measured in one run, as a profile defines them.

estimator.description: Estimator every compared value was computed with.

identity_schema.description: Identity-policy schema under which series membership and comparability were decided.

local_only.description: True when any input is not clean; such a comparison never promotes into tracked history.

run_key.description: Run mode: the run both sides were measured in.

profile.description: Run mode: the comparison profile the run was checked against (benchmark-result-schema.md section 5.5).

varying.description: Run mode: path of the coordinate whose value distinguishes the sides, such as provenance.subject_tree or coordinates.workload.parameters.role.

baseline.description: Run mode: the reference side, as its value of the varying coordinate.

contender.description: Run mode: the target side. Absent when a failed invariant prevented identifying it.

sides.description: Run mode: what each side declared about how it was built and entered, recorded as given and never judged, beside the environment the runner observed for it.

pairing.description: Run mode: how the two sides' attempts are paired.
pairing.$comment: Only paired comparison is defined; comparator.md open question 2 asks whether an unpaired method should be allowed.

failed_invariants.description: Run mode: profile invariants the run did not satisfy.

units.description: One evaluation each: a series point in history mode, a workload variant and quantity in run mode.

missing.description: Expected targets with no result, such as a side absent from a run or a series with no result from a batch request's target.

exclusions.description: Results left out of the evidence, with the reason.

method.description: Comparison method: a stable name and version, the effect measure it reports, and its complete configuration, such as k and minimum evidence.

effect_measure.description: How effect is measured from the reference estimate, such as relative, absolute, ratio, or log-ratio.

outcome.description: What one evaluation found. Shared by both unit kinds.

reference_estimate.description: Expected value from the reference points or the baseline side.

effect.description: Change from the reference estimate, in the method's effect measure.

noise.description: Variation on the effect's scale. Absent for a deterministic quantity.

noise_source.description: Where the noise came from, such as reference-points or paired-rounds.

provisional.description: True when the noise came from a provisional rule rather than evidence.

threshold.description: The effect magnitude the method required to indicate a change.

reason.description: Why the verdict is indeterminate, such as insufficient-history or duplicate-points.

unmatched_differences.description: Reported facts the identity policy or profile did not require to match, named by JSON Pointer into the reported coordinates, whose values differ between target and reference, such as /coordinates/environment/facts/os/kernel.

caveats.description: Quality caveats the reader should see.

runUnit.description: One workload variant and quantity, its two sides paired by round.

series.description: The series each side's results belong to, when the store assigns them one. Run mode reads no history from them.

historyUnit.description: One target series point against preceding points of its series.

series.description: Series fingerprint of the target and every reference point.

reference.description: The reference points the reference estimate was formed from, oldest first.

ordering.description: How the reference points were ordered before the target. Absent when no order was available.

boundaries.description: Resets, change points, and continuity joins that truncated or joined the reference.

side.description: A value of the varying coordinate, such as a tree id, a label, or a parameter value.

declared.description: One side's declared text, copied from its results' provenance.info, and the allowlisted environment variables observed for it.

invariant.description: Name of the invariant, such as alternation or equal-attempts.

workload.description: The unit it affects, when it affects only one.

side.description: Run mode: the side with no result.

workload.description: Workload variant: a named operation plus one parameter assignment.

estimator.description: Estimator declaration, as in the measurement-result schema.

resultRef.description: Stable reference to a stored result.
